title: Results of a Longitudinal Study of individuals with severe obesity before and after Bariatric Surgery
summary:
Weight Reduction Surgery (Metabolic and Bariatric surgery; MBS) is a life-changing treatment. However, long-term effects on patients’ mental wellbeing, romantic relationship and life satisfaction require further research. 

Hence, this study aims to determine how patients’ relationship- and life satisfaction, eating behavior,  depression level and ability to work change over the seven to ten year period following MBS-induced weight loss.

To assess the issue, patients are asked to answer a few questions about themselves, their living conditions, their ability to work, their life satisfaction, their eating habits, their relationship and depressive symptoms. Patients have the option of completing the questionnaires either online (via Lime Survey) or on paper (by post).
conditions: Obesity, grade II or III (BMI > 35), patients aged 18 years or older

interventions.name: Formerly severely obese patients who underwent bariatric surgery between September 2015 and June 2018 will be asked to complete the following standardised questionnaires on relevant psychosocial factors on a one-off basis: Work Ability Index (WAI; work ability), Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9;

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
preoperative body mass index (BMI) above 35 kg/m2, indicating an obesity grade of 2 or 3
Exclusion criteria:
- insufficient German language skills
- intellectual disability
- developmental or learning disorders
- history of prior bariatric surgery
- current substance abuse
